paper_title: New Limit on Axion-Like Dark Matter using Cold Neutrons
suggested_experiment_name: Beam EDM (cold neutron Ramsey apparatus at PSI/ILL)
coupling_convention: C_G / f_a in GeV^-1, as plotted on y-axis. This represents the ALP-gluon coupling strength normalized by the ALP decay constant. The plotted quantity is directly related to the neutron EDM oscillation amplitude via equation (1) in the paper: d_n^osc(t) = ±2.4 × 10^-16 e·cm · (C_G/f_a) · a_0 cos(m_a t), where a_0 is the local dark matter density oscillation amplitude and m_a is the ALP mass (converted to frequency via ω = m_a c^2 / ℏ on the top x-axis).
notes: Paper constrains ALP-gluon coupling via oscillating neutron EDM induced by dark matter axion-like particles. The best limit C_G/f_a m_a = 2.7 × 10^13 GeV^-2 (95% C.L.) is stated for the mass range 2×10^-17 to 2×10^-14 eV. The paper reports a mass-independent (flat) bound valid over the range 10^-19 to 4×10^-12 eV. The coupling is expressed as C_G/f_a m_a (product of coupling and mass), which is mass-dependent in the sense that the limit applies to this product. However, the paper presents the best limit as a single value valid over a broad mass range (2×10^-17 to 2×10^-14 eV), suggesting a roughly flat exclusion in the C_G/f_a m_a plane over this range. The data points encode this as a horizontal line from the lower to upper mass bound of the stated validity range. The local dark matter density ρ_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 is explicitly assumed (standard galactic halo model). The paper also discusses stochastic dark matter with a scaling factor of 3.2±0.3, but the primary reported limit is for deterministic dark matter. Extraction confidence is 0.75 because: (1) coupling type is unambiguous (ALP-gluon coupling manifesting as oscillating neutron EDM), (2) the numerical limit is clearly stated in the abstract and text, but (3) the exact mass dependence of the limit is somewhat subtle—the paper reports a best limit valid over a range rather than a detailed exclusion curve with many points, and the coupling convention (C_G/f_a m_a) is non-standard and requires careful interpretation. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 64)) | Vision: Figure 4 shows limits on ALP-gluon coupling C_G/f_a as a function of ALP mass (bottom x-axis in eV) and oscillation frequency (top x-axis in Hz). The y-axis is C_G/f_a in GeV^-1 on a log scale from 10^-24 to 10^-3. The Beam EDM exclusion region (pink/magenta shaded area with black dotted boundary) represents the primary constraint from this work. The boundary was traced by sampling densely in regions of high curvature (low mass, where the boundary rises steeply) and more sparsely in the high-mass region where the boundary flattens. The conversion from oscillation frequency to mass uses ω = m_a c^2 / ℏ, giving m_a [eV] ≈ 4.136 × 10^-15 × f [Hz]. The dark matter density ρ_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 was assumed in deriving the coupling limits. The paper reports a best limit of C_G/f_a = 2.7 × 10^13 GeV^-2 (95% C.L.) in the frequency range 5 mHz to 5 Hz, corresponding to ALP masses from ~10^-19 to ~10^-14 eV. Additional constraints from other experiments (nEDM, HfH, BBN, SN1987A, QCD axion line) are shown for context but not extracted here. | Calibration: No calibration needed
